newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargoes stall, barges trade steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargoes stall, barges trade steady.

text.p: NWE physical gas oil trade was slow and premiums were mixed on Thursday with a seasonal slump in volume braking both barge and cargo activity, traders said.
Speculators selling gasoline in the U.S. ahead of the contract's expiry helped push August IPE gas oil $1.75 lower to trade last at $169.25 a tonne.
The only steady physical volume was on the ARA barge market, where prompt parcels of heating oil changed hands at premiums ranging between 50 and $1 to August IPE.
Early talk had seen offers of up to $1.50 over August IPE for first half August.
A parcel of heating oil for second half August was heard done at a 75 cent premium. Diesel moved several times at the unchanged premium of $4 over August IPE.
Cargo activity has shrunk with the absence of key traders on holiday, lack of arbitrage opportunities to South America or the Far East and the high dollar value against the mark.
German barge buyers remained reluctant to show with the U.S. currency almost daily nudging seven year highs.
Diesel premiums were firm at around $4/$5.25 for first half August and around Sep IPE +$4/4.75 for second half August. Heat was slightly stronger at Aug IPE +$1/2.
